concepts.name: Purpose of three statements
concepts.summary: Recall what the income statement, balance sheet and cash flow statement each report and the question each answers about a company.

concepts.name: Income statement structure
concepts.summary: Explain how revenue flows down through costs and expenses to gross profit, operating profit and net income.

concepts.name: Balance sheet structure
concepts.summary: Describe how assets, liabilities and equity are grouped into current and non-current items at a point in time.

concepts.name: Cash flow statement sections
concepts.summary: Distinguish operating, investing and financing cash flows and what kinds of transactions fall in each.

concepts.name: Profit versus cash
concepts.summary: Explain why net income and cash generated in a period differ because of accrual accounting.

concepts.name: Ratio as a comparison
concepts.summary: State that a ratio divides one statement figure by another to make companies and periods comparable regardless of size.

misconceptions.text: Net income is the same as the cash a company has received during the period.
A large profit means the company has a large cash balance.
The balance sheet shows performance over a year just like the income statement.

concepts.name: Profit margin ratios
concepts.summary: Calculate gross, operating and net margins and interpret what each says about pricing and cost control.

concepts.name: Liquidity ratios
concepts.summary: Compute current and quick ratios and interpret a firm's ability to meet short-term obligations.

concepts.name: Return on assets and equity
concepts.summary: Calculate ROA and ROE and explain what they show about how efficiently capital generates profit.

concepts.name: Leverage ratios
concepts.summary: Compute debt-to-equity and interest coverage and interpret how much a firm relies on borrowing.

concepts.name: Activity turnover ratios
concepts.summary: Calculate inventory, receivables and asset turnover and read them as measures of operating efficiency.

concepts.name: Horizontal and vertical analysis
concepts.summary: Apply year-over-year change and common-size percentages to spot trends and changes in statement composition.

concepts.name: Free cash flow basics
concepts.summary: Calculate operating cash flow less capital expenditure and explain it as cash available after maintaining the asset base.

misconceptions.text: A higher current ratio is always better.
A single ratio for one year is enough to judge a company.
Debt is always bad, so a lower debt-to-equity ratio always signals a better company.

concepts.name: DuPont decomposition
concepts.summary: Break ROE into net margin, asset turnover and financial leverage to diagnose what drives returns.

concepts.name: Cash conversion cycle
concepts.summary: Combine days inventory, receivables and payables to analyse how efficiently working capital turns into cash.

concepts.name: Earnings quality assessment
concepts.summary: Compare operating cash flow with net income and examine accruals to judge how sustainable and reliable reported earnings are.

concepts.name: Peer and industry benchmarking
concepts.summary: Select appropriate peers and adjust for industry norms and accounting differences before comparing ratios.

concepts.name: Debt capacity and solvency
concepts.summary: Analyse net debt, EBITDA-based leverage and coverage together with maturities to assess ability to service debt.

concepts.name: Footnote and disclosure reading
concepts.summary: Use notes on accounting policies, debt, leases and segments to explain and qualify the face-statement numbers.

concepts.name: Non-recurring item adjustment
concepts.summary: Identify one-off gains, write-downs and restructuring charges and adjust earnings to reflect recurring performance.

misconceptions.text: A high ROE always means a highly profitable and healthy business.
Ratios can be compared directly between any two companies regardless of industry or accounting policy.
EBITDA is equivalent to cash flow.

concepts.name: Accounting policy comparability
concepts.summary: Evaluate how choices such as inventory method, depreciation and revenue recognition distort comparisons and restate to a common basis.

concepts.name: Lease and off-balance-sheet adjustments
concepts.summary: Adjust debt, assets and coverage ratios for leases and other obligations to reflect true leverage.

concepts.name: Red flags for manipulation
concepts.summary: Evaluate warning signs such as receivables outpacing sales, aggressive capitalisation and persistent gaps between profit and cash.

concepts.name: Return on invested capital analysis
concepts.summary: Assess ROIC against cost of capital to judge whether growth creates or destroys value.

concepts.name: Segment and geographic analysis
concepts.summary: Analyse segment margins, growth and capital use to see which parts drive consolidated results.

concepts.name: Sustainable growth and funding
concepts.summary: Judge whether growth can be funded from retained earnings and operating cash or depends on external capital.

concepts.name: Forecast-based ratio stress testing
concepts.summary: Project statements under downside scenarios and evaluate effects on liquidity, covenants and coverage.

misconceptions.text: If statements are audited and comply with standards, accounting-policy differences do not affect comparability.
Positive net income and growing revenue show that growth is creating value.
Manipulation shows up only as outright fraud, so compliant statements need no scepticism.

concepts.name: Integrated firm assessment
concepts.summary: Synthesise profitability, liquidity, leverage, cash generation and earnings quality into a defensible overall judgement and know which evidence outweighs the rest.

concepts.name: Sector-specific analytical frameworks
concepts.summary: Evaluate when standard ratios fail, as in banks or asset-light and cyclical firms, and choose sector-appropriate metrics.

concepts.name: Analytical model design
concepts.summary: Design a repeatable framework or scorecard that combines adjusted metrics and trends for screening or credit decisions.

concepts.name: Linking statements to valuation
concepts.summary: Translate normalised earnings, reinvestment and returns into forecast assumptions that feed a valuation or credit view.

concepts.name: Standards and regime differences
concepts.summary: Evaluate how differing accounting standards and regulatory regimes change reported figures and conclusions in cross-border comparison.

concepts.name: Communicating analytical conclusions
concepts.summary: Construct a clear, evidence-based, caveated recommendation that reconciles conflicting signals for decision-makers.

misconceptions.text: A single well-chosen model or ratio set works for every industry.
Sophisticated statement analysis removes the need for judgement about uncertain forecasts.
Moving between IFRS and US GAAP only changes presentation, not the numbers.
